To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extracellular matrix (1) induces neurite outgrowth from embryonic and pheochromcytoma cells and (2) promotes the survival of embryonal sensory neurons.

the extracellular matrix (a) induces cell attachment, flattening, and neurite outgrowth in PC12 and embryonic chicken sensory cells; (b) supports the survival of embryonal sensory cells in primary culture; and (c) induces neurite outgrowth by a mechanism involving the ECM and its carbohydrate components.

the extracellular matrix (1) induces cell attachment and morphogenesis in a variety of cell types, (2) supports the survival of embryonal sensory cells, and (3) induces neurite extension in both PC-12 cells and embryonal sensory neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of extracellular matrix in the development of the nervous system.
the induction of cell processes in embryonic chicken dorsal root ganglia neurons and PC-12 pheochromoctoma cells.
the role of extracellular matrix in the development, maintenance and regeneration of nerve fibers and the mechanisms by which the matrix exerts its influence on neuronal differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ECM is a potent and specific inducer of cell attachment, cell flattening and neuritogenesis in embryonic sensory cells and PC-12 cells.
the ECM is a potent morphogenetic agent that induces the formation of neurites in a variety of neuronal cell types.
the extracellular matrix is an active participant in the regulation of neuronal development and differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ECM is a natural substrate which induces neurite extension and cell attachment in a way similar or identical to that observed on substrates coated with ECM components.
the ECM is a potent inducer of cell attachment, flattening, and differentiation in a variety of cell types and that the ECM may play a role in the regulation of neuronal differentiation.
NGF is a necessary factor for the survival of PC-12 cells but that it is not sufficient to induce neurite outgrowth and that the ECM is a necessary substrate for the induction of neurites by NGF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ECM is a key factor in cell differentiation.
the extracellular matrix (or basement membrane) is not just a passive scaffold for the growth of cells, but that it actively directs the behavior of cells and their growth.
PC-12 cells and embryonic sensory neurons respond to ECM in a manner similar and different to their response to NGF.
